ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a single-phase AC power source, labeled as 230 V (RMS), 50 Hz; the upper end of the power source is connected in series with a thyristor/SCR with a gate, the right side is connected to a resistive load R, the output voltage v0 is marked across the resistor, with polarity positive at the top and negative at the bottom. Therefore this is a single-phase half-wave phase-controlled rectifier circuit, and the load is purely resistive. Reasoning: The input voltage RMS value is 230 V, so the source peak value Vm = 230√2 ≈ 325 V. For a resistive load, after the thyristor is triggered in the positive half-cycle, the output voltage follows the source instantaneous value Vm sinθ from the firing angle α to π. If α is before 90°, the output will contain the source peak value 325 V; but the output instantaneous peak value given in the problem is only 230 V, less than 325 V, so the firing angle should be after 90°. At this time, the maximum output value occurs at the just-triggered θ = α. Thus Vm sinα = 230, that is, 230√2 sinα = 230, sinα = 1/√2. Since α is located in the second quadrant, α = 135°.

method.method_draft: First identify from the figure that this is a single-phase half-wave phase-controlled rectifier with an SCR in series with a resistor, supplied by 230 V RMS AC. Convert the source RMS voltage to peak: Vm = 230√2 V. For an R load, the output follows the source only from firing angle α to π in each positive half-cycle. Because the required peak output is only 230 V, less than the source peak 325 V, the SCR must be fired after the source waveform peak, so the maximum output is the value at θ = α. Set Vm sin α = 230 and use α in quadrant II to obtain α ≈ 135°.
